```text
#56 is ab-wm's central keyboard-shortcut registry. The user's #57 (`?` dialog), #60 (turn shortcuts off) and #95 (`r` quote reply) all build on it. #65 does not, so it can start first. See [[sprint2-deliverables]].

**Merged 2026-10-19** via PR #96 (as of 10-22 ab-wm's open PR #97 for #58 adds `initShortcutLink`, an additive change), so #57, #58, #59 and #95 are unblocked; #60 is still blocked by #57. Branch from `main` now.

**State on 2026-10-18 (history):** the code was on branch `origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, with the last commit on 10-18. It had no PR and was not merged. ab-wm's spec reviews on all four issues said to "pay attention to the changes introduced by #56".

**API on that branch** (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`):
- `registerShortcut({keys, description, section?, element?, action})` registers a shortcut. `keys` is a space-separated sequence, such as `"g c"`. `description` and `section` arrive already translated from the server, through data attributes or a placeholder. A shortcut with an `element` lives only while that element is connected. Exact or prefix clashes throw.
- `getShortcuts()` returns the list that #57's dialog reads.
- `handleKeyDown` is the only dispatch point, where #60's off switch goes. It skips inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable, modifier keys, and events another handler already prevented.
- `initShortcutKbd` registers `s` and `t` from `<kbd>` hints, under the section "Repository". Nothing registers `?` yet.
- Unit tests are in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.

**Why:** ab-wm owns #56, and the API can change before it merges. The specs for #57, #60 and #95 name these functions, so a rename means updating those issue bodies too.

**How to apply:** before implementing #57, #60 or #95, check the state live. Use `gh pr list --search 56` and `git log origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, and re-read `shortcut.ts`. Branch from `main` only after #56 merges; never merge ab-wm's branch into the user's own branch (COURSE-WORKFLOW). If #56 is late, raise it with ab-wm early, because a sprint with no merged PR scores 0.

AGENTS.md has the base rules: Conventional Commits, the `Assisted-by:` trailer only, approval for each commit, and the issue number in the subject. Beyond those:

- **Trailer form:** `Assisted-by: Claude Code:<session model id>`, for example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`.
- **Editing a PR body:** `gh pr edit --body-file` replaces the whole body. Keep the `Closes #N` line and any image URLs.
- **Tech Debt section (from Sprint 2):** every PR body needs `## Tech Debt` with `**Introduced:**` and `**Encountered:**` lines; "None." is valid. Missing it costs D4 points. See [[sprint2-requirements]].
- **No stacked PRs:** COURSE-WORKFLOW forbids basing a PR on another feature branch or merging one into another. For a dependent issue (#60 needs #57), build it locally on top of #57 without pushing; after #57 merges, rebase that unpushed work onto `main`, then push and open the PR. See [[sprint2-deliverables]].
- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch`** closes any PR based on the deleted branch instead of retargeting it (tested 2026-10-24). The course repo has `delete_branch_on_merge=false`.
- **Screenshots required:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` wants UI screenshots on PRs. Show "after" only for a new feature, and before and after otherwise.

Hosting screenshots:
- `gh` can't mint `github.com/user-attachments/...` URLs; only the web UI uploads there.
- Commit the images under `docs/sprint<N>/screenshots/` (since 2026-10-24). Not under `ai-logs/`: `.coderabbit.yaml`'s PR-description check fails any link into `ai-logs/`, screenshots included (it flagged PR #115; Sprint 1's #71/#74 predate the check).
- Reference them as `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/<full-commit-sha>/<path>?raw=1`. Use the SHA as pushed: an amend or squash before the push changes it, and the old link 404s. Pin the SHA, not the branch, so the images survive branch deletion.

Taking screenshots (done for PR #71):
- Use headless Chromium with `colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark'` and `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, then `page.screenshot` with a `clip`.
- Read each image back to check the crop.
- Rebuild first, or the footer shows a stale version.
- After pushing, confirm each `?raw=1` URL returns 200 as an image.

**Why:** The course fork diverges from default attribution, and these screenshot details each cost a retry.
**How to apply:** Use with [[verify-skill]] for the capture. Commit identity is in [[course-repo-and-identity]].
```

```text
Character-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4)
OPEN
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged) and #57 · starts when #57's dialog exists

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts, so that a word I dictate does not run a shortcut and move me away from what I was doing.

## User Scenario
A voice control user is on a repository page. Each time they dictate a word, focus jumps into the code search box. They press `?` and find a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog labelled "Enable character key shortcuts". They clear it, and the listed shortcuts turn grey. They close the dialog and dictate without interruption. The next time they open Gitea in that browser, shortcuts are still off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the user has cleared the "Enable character key shortcuts" checkbox in #57's dialog, when they press a registered shortcut other than `?`, then no shortcut runs. Focus stays where it was, and the key press is not default-prevented. For example, `s` on a repository home page does nothing.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are off, when the user reloads the page or opens another page in the same browser, then shortcuts are still off.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `?`, then the dialog still opens. The user can turn shortcuts back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are off, when the user checks the box again, then `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser where storage access throws an error, when a page loads, then shortcuts are on, the checkbox is checked, and no uncaught error occurs.
- [ ] AC6: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `g` and then another key, then the registry does not hold `g` as the start of a sequence, and neither key runs a shortcut.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the checkbox label comes from a locale key.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6. The e2e test from #57 gains a check for AC2.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the setting on the server, or syncing it across browsers.
- A copy of the setting on the user settings pages.
- Keys that widgets own, such as the code editor's keys and the type-to-jump keys in menus. #56 already leaves these keys alone.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 accepts three options: turn off, remap, or active only on focus. This issue picks "turn off" as the smallest complete option. Reviewer to confirm this reading.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: store the setting in the browser
**Decision:** Store the setting with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper in `web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`, under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled`, with a default of `true`. Before it runs a shortcut, `handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` reads the setting. `handleKeyDown` is the registry's only dispatch point.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A per-user server setting in the existing `user_setting` key-value table (`models/user/setting.go`), with a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
- (b) A cookie that the server reads, so that the server leaves the shortcut hints out of the page when shortcuts are off.

**Rationale:** Shortcuts also work for signed-out visitors, and option (a) has nowhere to store a signed-out visitor's choice. The preference also belongs to one machine. Someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off on every machine. Option (b) lets the server skip the hints, but the browser then sends the cookie with every request, and a behaviour that lives in the browser needs a server change. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.

**Consequences:** The server does not change. The setting does not follow the user to another browser, and support staff cannot see it.

### Decision 2: keep `?` working when shortcuts are off
**Decision:** The setting turns off every character shortcut except `?`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Turn off every shortcut, `?` included. This is the most literal reading of SC 2.1.4.
- (b) Use SC 2.1.4's "active only on focus" option, so that shortcuts run only while one component has focus.

**Rationale:** With option (a), a keyboard-only user who turns shortcuts off has no keyboard path back to the checkbox. Option (a) swaps one accessibility failure for another. One exempt key is the usual way back. Option (b) suits a widget's own keys, but Gitea's shortcuts act on the whole page. For example, `s` moves focus to the code search box from anywhere on the page. If shortcuts worked only inside one component, they would lose their purpose.

**Consequences:** `?` stays active as a deliberate exception. The check carries a short code comment that says why, so that nobody removes the exception later. A user who dictates "?" still opens the dialog. The dialog does no harm and closes with Escape.

## Scope
```

```text
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field, or belongs to an open dialog, not the page behind it
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable || document.querySelector('dialog[open]')) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

// Groups shortcuts by section in the order each section first appears, the default section first.
// A shortcut without a section belongs to the default one.
export function groupShortcuts(shortcuts: ShortcutInfo[], defaultSection: string): Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]> {
  const groups = new Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]>([[defaultSection, []]]);
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    const section = shortcut.section ?? defaultSection;
    if (!groups.has(section)) groups.set(section, []);
    groups.get(section)!.push(shortcut);
  }
  return groups;
}

function renderShortcutKeys(keys: string): string {
  return keys.split(' ').map((key) => html`<kbd>${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`).join('');
}

// the help dialog lists the shortcuts registered when it opens, so it also shows ones added after page load
export function initShortcutHelp(dialog: HTMLDialogElement) {
  const general = dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section')!;
  registerShortcut({
    keys: dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: general,
    element: dialog,
    action: () => {
      const groups = groupShortcuts(getShortcuts(), general);
      dialog.querySelector('.shortcut-help-sections')!.innerHTML = Array.from(groups, ([section, shortcuts]) => html`
        <section>
          <h3>${section}</h3>
          <dl>${htmlRaw(shortcuts.map((s) => html`<div class="shortcut-help-row"><dt>${s.description}</dt><dd>${htmlRaw(renderShortcutKeys(s.keys))}</dd></div>`).join(''))}</dl>
        </section>
      `).join('');
      const opener = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      dialog.addEventListener('close', () => opener.focus(), {once: true}); // browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes
      dialog.showModal();
    },
  });
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutHelp', initShortcutHelp);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}
/* eslint-disable no-restricted-globals */
// Some people deploy Gitea under a subpath, so it needs prefix to avoid local storage key conflicts.
// And these keys are for user settings only, it also needs a specific prefix,
// in case in the future there are other uses of local storage, and/or we need to clear some keys when the quota is exceeded.
const itemKeyPrefix = 'gitea:setting:';

function handleLocalStorageError(e: any) {
  // in the future, maybe we need to handle quota exceeded errors differently
  console.error('Error using local storage for user settings', e);
}

function getLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string): string | null {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    const legacyValue = localStorage?.getItem(legacyKey) ?? null;
    const value = localStorage?.getItem(itemKey) ?? null; // avoid undefined
    if (value !== null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // if both values exist, remove the legacy one
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    } else if (value === null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // migrate legacy value to new key
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
      localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, legacyValue);
      return legacyValue;
    }
    return value;
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
  return null;
}

function setLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string, value: string) {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, value);
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
}

export const localUserSettings = {
  getString: (key: string, def: string = ''): string => {
    return getLocalStorageUserSetting(key) ?? def;
  },
  setString: (key: string, value: string) => {
    setLocalStorageUserSetting(key, value);
  },
  getBoolean: (key: string, def: boolean = false): boolean => {
    return localUserSettings.getString(key, String(def)) === 'true';
  },
  setBoolean: (key: string, value: boolean) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, String(value));
  },
  getJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, def: T): T => {
    const value = getLocalStorageUserSetting(key);
    try {
      const decoded = value !== null ? JSON.parse(value) : null;
      return {...def, ...decoded};
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`Unable to parse JSON value for local user settings ${key}=${value}`, e);
    }
    return def;
  },
  setJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, value: T) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, JSON.stringify(value));
  },
};

window.localUserSettings = localUserSettings;
```

```text
import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, groupShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutHelp, initShortcutKbd, initShortcutLink} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)

  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();

  });

  });

  test('AC4 a sequence runs once and its keys run no single-key shortcut', () => {

  });

  test('AC9 listing gives keys, description and section of the shortcuts on the page', () => {

describe('groupShortcuts', () => {
  test('#57 AC5 groups by section in order of first appearance, the default section first', () => {

// the markup of templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl and RepoFileSearch.vue
function renderHint(key: string, placeholder: string, section?: string) {
  const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
  wrapper.className = 'ui input global-shortcut-wrapper';
  wrapper.innerHTML = `<input placeholder="${placeholder}"><kbd data-shortcut-keys="${key}">${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`;
  document.body.append(wrapper);
  const input = wrapper.querySelector('input')!;
  const kbd = wrapper.querySelector('kbd')!;
  if (section) kbd.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  initShortcutKbd(kbd);
  return {wrapper, input, kbd};
}

// the markup of templates/base/footer.tmpl
function renderHelpDialog() {
  const dialog = document.createElement('dialog');
  dialog.setAttribute('data-shortcut-keys', '?');
  dialog.setAttribute('data-shortcut-description', 'Show keyboard shortcuts');
  dialog.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'General');
  dialog.innerHTML = `<form method="dialog"><h2>Keyboard shortcuts</h2><button aria-label="Close">x</button></form><div class="shortcut-help-sections"></div>`;
  document.body.append(dialog);
  initShortcutHelp(dialog);
  return dialog;
}

// a tab link, whose text also holds an open count
function renderLink(keys: string, href: string, description: string, section?: string, shortcutHref?: string) {
  const link = document.createElement('a');
  link.href = href;
  link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-keys', keys);
  link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-description', description);
  if (section) link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  if (shortcutHref) link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-href', shortcutHref);
  link.innerHTML = `${description} <span class="ui small label">3</span>`;
  document.body.append(link);
  initShortcutLink(link);
  return link;
}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, assertNoJsError, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

async function createRepo(page: Page) {
  const repoName = `e2e-shortcut-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, repoName, 'other.txt', 'other file');
  return `/${env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER}/${repoName}`;
}

// presses a shortcut that leaves the page, and waits until the next page can take one
async function goWith(page: Page, keys: string, url: RegExp) {
  for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(url);
  await page.waitForLoadState();
}

test('s and t focus their boxes, and Escape clears them', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  const searchHint = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd');
  const goToFile = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container input');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the Vue box has mounted and registered
  await expect(searchHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');

  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.type('st');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('st');
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('');
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeVisible();

  await page.keyboard.press('t');
  await expect(goToFile).toBeFocused();
  await expect(goToFileHint).toBeHidden();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('a key the language menu uses for type-ahead runs no shortcut', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd')).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 's'); // s is a live shortcut here
  await page.locator('aria-menu:has(.language-menu) > button').focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // jumps to a language starting with "s", such as Suomi
  await expect(page.locator('.language-menu .item:focus')).toHaveText(/^s/i);
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]')).not.toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('t keeps working after moving through the file tree', async ({page}) => {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/src/branch/main/README.md`); // the file tree is shown by default
  const goToFile = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container input');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');

  for (const [file, content] of [['other.txt', 'other file'], ['README.md', 'e2e-shortcut-']]) {
    await page.locator(`#view-file-tree .tree-item[title="${file}"]`).click();
    await expect(page.locator('.file-view')).toContainText(content); // the page content was swapped
    await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the new hint has registered
    await page.keyboard.press('t');
    await expect(goToFile).toBeFocused();
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  }
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g shortcuts go to the repository tabs, and g c to the default branch', async ({page}) => {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
  await apiCreateBranch(page.request, owner, repoName, 'feature');
  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/src/branch/feature`);
  const issuesTab = page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g i"]');
  await expect(issuesTab).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-description', 'Issues'); // the tab's text also holds its open count
  await expect(issuesTab).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g c"]')).toHaveAttribute('href', `${repoLink}/src/branch/feature`);

  await goWith(page, 'g c', new RegExp(`${repoLink}$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g i', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/issues$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g p', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/pulls$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g a', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/actions$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g w', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/wiki$`));
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g shortcuts are missing for tabs that are not shown or that leave Gitea', async ({page}) => {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
  await apiEditRepo(page.request, owner, repoName, {
    has_pull_requests: false,
    has_actions: false,
    has_issues: true,
    external_tracker: {external_tracker_url: 'https://tracker.example.com/'},
    has_wiki: true,
    external_wiki: {external_wiki_url: 'https://wiki.example.com/'},
  });
  await page.goto(repoLink);
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-items a[href="https://tracker.example.com/"]')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-items a[href="https://wiki.example.com/"]')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys^="g "]')).toHaveCount(1); // only g c

  for (const keys of ['g i', 'g p', 'g a', 'g w']) {
    for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
  }
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // a live shortcut still runs after them
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]')).toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g shortcuts work for tabs moved into the "more" menu', async ({page}) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({width: 420, height: 800});
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  await page.goto(repoLink);
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-popup [data-shortcut-keys="g w"]')).toBeAttached(); // the Wiki tab no longer fits
  await goWith(page, 'g w', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/wiki$`));
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g n goes to notifications when signed in, outside any repository', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto('/explore/repos');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g n"]')).toHaveCount(0); // signed out
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/explore/repos');
  const bell = page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g n"]');
  await expect(bell).toHaveCount(1); // the bell is in the page twice, only one copy declares it
  await expect(bell).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-description', 'Notifications');
  await expect(bell).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'General');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys^="g "]')).toHaveCount(1); // no repository shortcuts outside a repository
  await goWith(page, 'g n', /\/notifications$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('? opens a dialog of the page\'s shortcuts, and Escape returns focus', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd')).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the Vue box has mounted and registered

  await search.focus();
  await page.keyboard.type('a?');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('a?'); // typed into the box, no dialog
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', {name: 'Keyboard shortcuts'});
  await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape'); // clears and leaves the box

  const opener = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top form button');
  await opener.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('?');
  await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
  await expect(dialog.getByRole('heading', {name: 'General'})).toBeVisible();
  await expect(dialog.locator('.shortcut-help-row')).toContainText(['Show keyboard shortcuts', 'Search code…', 'Go to file']);

  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // the page behind the dialog takes no shortcuts
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('g'); // inertness alone stops s, but g i would navigate away and fail the focus check below
  await page.keyboard.press('i');
  await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();
  await expect(opener).toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});
```

```text
# i18n — locale files and translation

**Read when:** adding or changing any user-visible string.
**Not here:** using a key in a template -> `templates.md`; in TypeScript -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

The translated strings and the machinery that looks them up, for both the backend/templates and
the frontend.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **the only file you edit** — the source of truth |
| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | 28 other locales, all generated from Crowdin |
| `modules/translation/translation.go` | locale loading and lookup; requires the `locale_*.json` naming |
| `modules/translation/i18n/` | the lookup implementation and fallback behaviour |
| `crowdin.yml` | the sync config: source is `locale_en-US.json`, translations land as `locale_%locale%.json` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- A `data-` attribute carrying a translated string to TypeScript is read with `getAttribute` and
  usually named for its use (`data-tooltip-content`, read in `web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`). Vue
  mounts often use `data-locale-<name>`, as `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` does for
  both plural forms.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes

**Add a string.** Add the key to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` in the right group, use it via
`ctx.Locale.Tr` or `trN`, and leave the other locale files alone.

**Add a plural.** Two keys named `<key>_1` and `<key>_n` plus `TrN` / `trN`; the count argument
selects the form.

**Add a string the frontend needs.** Prefer a `data-` attribute or `pageData` from the handler.
Only genuinely general text belongs in the global `window.config.i18n` object.

## Gotchas
```

```bash
test('shortcuts turned off in the dialog stay off after a reload, and turn back on from the keyboard', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', {name: 'Keyboard shortcuts'});
  const toggle = dialog.getByRole('checkbox', {name: 'Enable character key shortcuts'});
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd')).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 's');

  await page.keyboard.press('?');
  await expect(toggle).toBeChecked();
  await toggle.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await expect(toggle).not.toBeChecked();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd')).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 's');
  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('?'); // still opens with shortcuts off
  await expect(toggle).not.toBeChecked();
  await toggle.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-25 05:07:46Z)**_

#60 is implemented and tested. It's local only, on the new branch `feat/issue-60-shortcut-toggle`, which I cut from #57's branch (PR #115). Nothing is committed or pushed.

**How it works**
- **The checkbox:** the `?` dialog now ends with "Enable character key shortcuts" (new locale key `shortcuts.help.enable`). Clearing it greys out every listed shortcut except `?`.
- **Turning shortcuts off:** shortcuts can now be marked `alwaysOn`, and only `?` is. When the setting is off, the registry ignores every other shortcut, so the key keeps its normal behaviour and `g` no longer starts a sequence (AC1, AC3, AC6).
- **Storage:** the setting is saved in the browser under `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled` and also kept in memory. Turning shortcuts back on takes effect without a reload (AC4). If the browser blocks storage, shortcuts start on and the checkbox still works for the current page (AC5).
- **Docs:** I added one line about the off switch to the shortcut recipe in `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` and to its guide twin. I re-wrapped both paragraphs so the files stay under their line caps.

**Tests**
- **Unit:** all 34 tests in `shortcut.test.ts` pass, including 7 new ones for #60. Vitest's environment has no usable `localStorage`, so the new tests stub it.
- **e2e:** the new test turns shortcuts off, reloads, checks `s` does nothing, then turns them back on from the keyboard. All 18 tests pass on Chromium and WebKit. The new test has to wait for focus to leave the closed dialog before pressing `s`, because Chromium can take that key before the dialog finishes closing.
- **Firefox:** all 9 Firefox tests failed locally. The browser crashes on startup on this Mac, and Firefox normally only runs in CI, so that result has to come from CI.
- **Lint:** `lint-js`, `lint-css` and `lint-templates` pass. `lint-json` fails only on `data/indexers/issues.bleve/index_meta.json`, a local runtime file that isn't in git.
- **`check.sh`:** it reports two failures, both line-cap overruns in `models-issues.md`, which was already over before this branch.

**Possible Tech Debt item for the PR:** with shortcuts off, the `S`/`T` hints in the search boxes and their `aria-keyshortcuts` attributes still show. The issue doesn't ask for this to change.

**Next steps:** after #115 merges, rebase this branch onto `main`, then commit (once you approve), push and open the PR. You'll also need to file this session's log with `specstory sync` and post the #60 AI Assistance comment.
